response.overview: In 1953, Roger Tory Peterson and British naturalist James Fisher took a 100-day, 30,000-mile journey across North America, starting in Newfoundland and ending in Alaska. Roger, who had seen every US state and grown accustomed to them, wished to share the joy of discovery with his dear friend. James Fisher would offer new reactions, new observations, to this vast continent. As Roger put it, “I would see America again through his eyes.”  "If you come to America," Roger Tory Peterson suggested, "I will meet you in Newfoundland and conduct you around the continent…you will see a more complete cross section of wild America than any other Englishman, and all but a few North Americans, have ever seen."  Their adventures and observations of this journey were later published in the 1955 book of the same name, Wild America.
response.title: WILD AMERICA
